nodes.content: Design a multi-tenant service load balancer that maintains fairness without retry-driven overload under delayed feedback and partial failures.
requirements: Under feasible demand, each tenant receives at least 90% of its weighted fair throughput.
During backend failures and five-second telemetry delays, retry amplification stays below 1.2 attempts per request.

nodes.content: Combine weighted deficit scheduling, local backend admission limits, failure-triggered circuit breakers, and 10% tenant retry budgets.
How should admission limits redistribute tenant capacity when a backend fails before five-second telemetry updates arrive?
Local error-triggered caps redirect traffic to healthy backends, preserving ≥90% weighted-fair throughput despite five-second telemetry lag when capacity suffices.
Specify 200-ms error-triggered caps and healthy-backend slot redistribution; simulate five-second telemetry lag, checking weighted throughput and attempts/request.
Run FairFailSim v1: one-of-four backend failure, 200-ms caps, feasible demand, five-second telemetry lag; measure fair-share attainment and attempts/request.
FairFailSim v1: minimum tenant fair-share attainment was 93%; retry amplification peaked at 1.12 attempts/request under five-second telemetry lag.
Compare 200-ms caps against telemetry-only caps in FairFailSim v2 with intermittent failures and five-second lag; measure fair-share attainment and attempts/request.
FairFailSim v2: intermittent failures yielded 84% minimum local-cap fair-share attainment despite spare capacity; telemetry-only achieved 91% but 1.31 attempts/request.
Do 200-ms cap resets strand healthy-backend slots during intermittent failures, explaining FairFailSim v2’s 84% fair-share attainment?
One-second local-cap hysteresis prevents stranded healthy slots during intermittent failures, restoring ≥90% fair-share attainment and <1.2 attempts/request.
Instrument healthy-slot occupancy and cap-reset events in FairFailSim v3; compare 200-ms resets with one-second hysteresis under intermittent failures.
Run FairFailSim v3 with five-second telemetry lag, comparing 200-ms resets and one-second hysteresis; log slot occupancy, fair-share attainment, attempts/request.
FairFailSim v3: 200-ms caps achieved 94% single-failure attainment; intermittent-failure hysteresis achieved 92%, 96% healthy-slot occupancy, and 1.14 attempts/request.
Replay BurstFail-48 traces; compare 200-ms resets and one-second hysteresis on healthy-slot occupancy, minimum fair-share attainment, and attempts/request.
BurstFail-48: hysteresis raised healthy-slot occupancy from 81% to 96%, but minimum fair-share attainment reached only 86%; attempts/request was 1.16.
Instrument BurstFail-48 per-tenant deficit balances and slot assignments under one-second hysteresis; identify why 96% occupancy yields only 86% fair-share attainment.
BurstFail-48: stale deficits caused transient 86% attainment; after one-second settling, all 48 failure traces sustained ≥92% fair-share and 1.16 attempts/request.
Keep one-second hysteresis; add deficit rebasing on slot changes to address transient 86% fairness despite 96% occupancy.
Rebase tenant deficits on healthy-slot changes, retain one-second admission hysteresis, and enforce 10% retry-token budgets behind circuit breakers.
Can deficit rebasing eliminate BurstFail-48’s transient 86% fair-share dip without exceeding 1.2 attempts/request during concurrent failures?
On BurstFail-48 concurrent failures, rebasing deficits on slot changes keeps minimum fair-share attainment ≥90% and attempts/request <1.2.
Replay concurrent-failure BurstFail-48 traces with and without deficit rebasing; compare minimum tenant fair-share attainment and attempts/request.
Run BurstFail-48 concurrent-failure replays with rebasing enabled versus disabled, logging per-tenant minimum fair-share attainment and peak attempts/request.
BurstFail-48 concurrent failures: rebasing raised minimum fair-share attainment from 86% to 91%; peak retry amplification remained 1.16 attempts/request.
Sweep feasible-load BurstFail-48 traces across tenant weights and two-backend flaps with five-second lag; measure rebased fair-share attainment and attempts/request.
BurstFail-48 two-backend flaps at 1:8 tenant weights: rebasing yielded 87% minimum fair-share attainment despite feasible capacity; peak attempts/request was 1.17.
Why does deficit rebasing still leave the 1:8-weight tenant at 87% fair-share attainment during two-backend flaps?
Rebasing erases low-weight tenants’ accrued deficit during flaps; preserving normalized credit should restore their fair-share attainment above 90%.
Log tenant deficit credit before each flap; compare zero-reset rebasing with weight-normalized credit preservation in 1:8 BurstFail-48 replays.
Replay 1:8 BurstFail-48 flaps with zero-reset versus normalized-credit rebasing; record lost low-weight credit, fair-share attainment, and attempts/request.
BurstFail-48: normalized-credit rebasing improved low-weight attainment only from 87% to 88%; lost credit was <1% of entitlement.
Trace denied low-weight requests during BurstFail-48 flaps, comparing normalized-credit preservation with and without per-tenant admission caps.
Capped BurstFail-48 replays: preserving normalized credit raised low-weight attainment from 87% to 92%; uncapped preservation reached 88%.
Why does normalized-credit preservation reach 92% low-weight attainment only when per-tenant admission caps are enabled?
Uncapped high-weight in-flight requests monopolize recovered slots; tenant caps unlock preserved credit, raising low-weight attainment to 92%.
Measure per-tenant in-flight occupancy and recovered-slot assignments across capped and uncapped BurstFail-48 replays with normalized-credit preservation.
Instrument BurstFail-48 slot handoffs: compare capped versus uncapped high-weight in-flight occupancy and low-weight assignments during two-backend recovery.
BurstFail-48: uncapped high-weight traffic took 95% of recovered slots versus 88% capped; low-weight assignments rose from 5% to 12%.
Sweep high-weight in-flight caps at 90%, 95%, and uncapped in BurstFail-48; measure recovered-slot shares, low-weight attainment, and attempts/request.
BurstFail-48: 90% cap yielded 12% low-weight recovered slots yet 88% attainment; 95% cap yielded 5% slots yet 92%.
Provisionally select the 95% high-weight cap for 92% low-weight attainment; investigate completion timing because slot share mispredicts fairness.
A 95% cap preserves fast-backend access for low-weight requests; 90% diverts more assignments to slower backends, reducing completions.
Compare low-weight fast-backend access, assignment latency, and completion rates under 90% versus 95% caps in BurstFail-48.
Replay BurstFail-48 at 90% and 95% caps; tag low-weight assignments by backend speed and record latency and completed throughput.
BurstFail-48: 95% cap sent 78% of low-weight assignments to fast backends versus 49% at 90%; completion latency fell 34%.
Adopt the 95% high-weight cap over 90%: low-weight fair-share attainment reaches 92%, aided by faster backend access.
Preserve normalized deficits, cap high-weight occupancy at 95%, retain one-second hysteresis, and enforce per-tenant 10% retry budgets.
Can replica-local 10% retry budgets keep aggregate attempts/request below 1.2 when failovers shift tenants between balancer replicas?
Replica-local retry budgets double-spend migrated requests across balancers, pushing aggregate attempts/request above 1.2 during failover.
Simulate three-balancer tenant migrations with five-second telemetry lag; compare replica-local versus request-scoped retry tokens by attempts per original request.
Run MigFail-3 with three balancers, backend failures, tenant migrations, and five-second lag; compare local versus request-scoped retry tokens.
MigFail-3: local budgets reached 1.27 attempts/original request after migrations; request-scoped tokens held 1.09 under identical failures.
Select MigFail-3’s 1.27-attempt local-budget case; trace migrated token grants and replay request-scoped suppression under synchronized migration.
MigFail-3 migration audit containing per-request token-grant timelines, duplicate-grant flags, and synchronized request-scoped replay traces.
Cross-check MigFail-3 audit against raw grants, then replay audited migrations to test p3’s ≥90% fairness and <1.2 attempts/request.
Audited MigFail-3 request-scoped replay achieved 91% minimum tenant fair-share attainment and 1.09 attempts/original request; no duplicate grants.
Replace replica-local retry budgets with migration-safe request-scoped tokens: local accounting reached 1.27 attempts/request; audited tokens yielded 1.09 and 91% fairness.
Use weighted deficit scheduling with normalized credit, 95% occupancy caps, one-second failure hysteresis, and migration-safe request-scoped retry tokens.
Can request-scoped tokens prevent duplicate retries when balancer replicas partition and receive the same request during five-second telemetry lag?
Partitioned replicas can each redeem request-scoped tokens without shared state, raising attempts/original request above 1.2 despite token limits.
Partition MigFail-3 balancers for five seconds; replay duplicate request IDs and compare independent token redemption against single-writer leases.
Run PartitionMig-5: duplicate request IDs across partitioned balancers with five-second lag; record token redemptions and attempts/original request.
PartitionMig-5: independent redemption duplicated 4% of retry tokens, but attempts/request stayed 1.17; minimum tenant fair-share attainment fell to 85%.
Defer p4: retain request-scoped tokens, but diagnose and correct PartitionMig-5’s 85% tenant fair-share attainment.
Use partition-stable tenant capacity reservations with local borrowing, normalized deficit accounting, and deterministic request-owner retry fencing.
Can partition-stable reservations maintain ≥90% tenant fair-share attainment when tenant demand shifts unevenly across isolated balancers?
With skewed arrivals, local borrowing cannot reclaim idle reservations across partitions, dropping minimum tenant fair-share attainment below 90%.
Extend PartitionMig-5 with 80:20 arrival skew; track stranded tenant reservations, minimum fair-share attainment, and attempts/original request.
Run PartitionMig-5 80:20 skew with local borrowing; log idle remote reservations, tenant completions, and attempts/request during five-second partitions.
PartitionMig-5 80:20 skew stranded 18% of reserved slots; minimum tenant fair-share attainment fell to 82%, with 1.15 attempts/request.
Replay MigFail-3 migration-audit requests with 80:20 partition skew; evaluate p5 fencing and reservations against 82% fairness and attempts/request.
Skewed audit replay: owner fencing reduced duplicate grants from 4% to zero and attempts/request to 1.10; fairness remained 82%.
Replay MigFail-3 audit with balanced partition arrivals; assess p5 owner fencing, reservation utilization, tenant fairness, and attempts/request.
Balanced-partition audit: owner fencing avoided duplicate retries, yet p5 minimum tenant fair-share attainment was 88% despite 97% reservation utilization.
Compare p5’s skewed and balanced audit replays, tracing per-tenant reservation ownership and completions behind 82% and 88% fairness.
Reservation traces: 22% of skewed versus 9% of balanced low-weight requests reached balancers lacking their reserved slots.
Reject fixed per-balancer tenant reservations for fairness; retain owner fencing, which removed duplicate retry grants without resolving misplaced-slot underdelivery.
Retain one-second hysteresis, normalized deficits, 95% caps, and owner-fenced request-scoped retries; reject fixed reservations pending partition-safe routing.
